findings.title: Specify controls that prevent production Git deployment before staging passes
findings.problem: Both existing Vercel projects use their production target and the plan commits/pushes one source revision, but no exact branch/auto-deployment/domain-assignment control is specified. If both projects follow main, the same push can release production before step7, bypassing the stated staging-first sequence. Disabling feature previews does not prevent this.
findings.requiredChange: Record each project Git binding, production branch and deployment-trigger control. Stage the exact production-target commit without assigning canonical domains, verify its isolated binding and immutable URL, then promote that tested production build. Prevent automatic production-domain assignment during staging verification; record prior deployment and safe rollback/first-launch disable procedure. Reconcile the operator-authorized two-project topology with effective TR20 rather than claiming the old Preview topology was executed.
findings.validation: Metadata preflight plus a dry-run/fake release-order test must prove a source push or staging failure cannot activate production; read back deployed commit/environment/domain after promotion.

findings.title: Bound scheduler history and quantify free-tier usage
findings.problem: A one-second pg_cron job runs86400 times/day even when no HTTP work exists. Supabase documents that cron.job_run_details grows for every execution and is not automatically cleaned. No retention/row budget is specified for this or new scheduler history. Idle HTTP suppression alone does not protect the500MB database. Continuous active one-second HTTP calls would be2592000/month before user traffic, beyond the currently documented1000000 Hobby invocations.
findings.requiredChange: Add explicit bounded retention/cleanup for this owned cron job and private scheduler outcome records, with cleanup ownership and failure behavior. Record actual plan/quota readback, expected active-room call/message/connection budget, backlog/DB-size thresholds and operator-visible graceful quota handling. Do not promise unlimited continuous load or bypass platform pausing.
findings.validation: Tests prove history remains bounded and cleanup never removes pending gameplay work; staging evidence shows idle HTTP count zero, bounded history, current quotas, and backlog/503 or429 recovery.

findings.title: Define scheduler secret and function trust boundaries beyond Vault storage
findings.problem: The plan restricts endpoint/secret changes to an administrator but does not specify read/execute grants. pg_net materializes decrypted Authorization headers in its request queue; Vault and extension ownership/default grants are platform-specific. Storing a credential in Vault is not proof that every database role is denied it. A newly created callable SECURITY DEFINER wrapper could also expose privileged dispatch.
findings.requiredChange: Inventory effective schema usage, object ownership, function EXECUTE and Vault/pg_net/control-table privileges. Put dispatcher/control objects in an unexposed private schema, use a fixed safe search_path and explicit allowlisted endpoint, revoke PUBLIC execution on owned wrappers, and prove anon/authenticated cannot inspect secrets or dispatch work. Identify trusted application/service/admin roles honestly; do not assert service_role cannot read Vault if its platform grants permit it. Keep the scheduler credential purpose-limited. Avoid unsupported blanket revocations of Supabase-owned extension objects.
findings.validation: Role-based SQL/API denial tests, secret-free cron command/history/readback, no exposed secret-returning function, endpoint-change denial, and callback authorization tests.

findings.title: Make the guarded scheduler recovery contract explicit
findings.problem: Private in-flight state and backoff are mentioned but their state machine and idle predicate are unspecified. pg_net request and response tables are unlogged, so a database restart or response expiry can leave durable in-flight state without a response. In current runtime, match bootstrap is a separate starts() query after lobby jobs; a room can already be started without an existing match or due job. A guard looking only at jobs/outbox could permanently miss that work.
findings.requiredChange: Define transactional guard acquisition, finite in-flight lease, HTTP timeout versus Vercel worker limit, bounded backoff and recovery for missing/evicted responses. Due-work detection must include eligible room-to-match bootstrap, due/expired-lease lobby and match jobs, and pending outbox. Do not mark application work complete based only on HTTP submission/timeout. Preserve independent deadline and publication outcomes.
findings.validation: Mock-first and disposable SQL tests for simultaneous ticks, idle suppression, startup gap, lost pg_net response/restart, late duplicate callback, worker503/429, outbox failure without deadline starvation, and eventual canonical recovery.

findings.title: Retain the required reproducible provisioning and environment contract
findings.problem: Effective TR23 requires a manually invoked repeatable provisioning script; the execution plan currently describes actions without naming its checked-in entry point or contracts. Generic renaming also omits the precise per-project variable-name/target/branch mapping and repeat-run/rotation behavior. Database URL handling is secure in principle but leaves the pooler/role/CA identity choice unresolved.
findings.requiredChange: Specify a version-controlled doctor/plan/apply/status procedure with pinned documented tools, migration hashes/history/drift checks and idempotent reruns. Add an allowlisted environment manifest mapping integration keys to WORDPAIRS_* names, target scopes, classification and rotation behavior; preserve sensitive type and verify no accidental Preview credential inheritance. Map database URL using an explicit approved host/user/database/port and CA strategy; strip only understood SSL parameters after verification or reject them, never weaken certificate checks. Select a serverless-compatible connection endpoint and verify project binding privately. Confirm hosted Realtime accepts the existing custom HS256 token and that its per-project signing key is available/valid before declaring live transport configured.
findings.validation: Dry-run has no writes; second apply makes no extra migration/job/secret; mismatch aborts before mutation; SSL/query override/CA/host and environment-scope negative tests; cross-project token/channel denial plus renewal.

findings.title: Resolve the existing free-tier eligibility prerequisite before production promotion
findings.problem: The plan acknowledges unverified Hobby eligibility for prize-contest use but still unconditionally advances to production in step7. Effective TR21 requires personal/non-commercial Hobby use. Current Vercel guidance defines commercial purpose broadly and directs uncertain cases to support; this review cannot turn the contest purpose into a provider ruling.
findings.requiredChange: Make the eligibility disposition an explicit technical/provider prerequisite for promotion: record a defensible current policy basis or actual provider clarification, or keep the eligibility-dependent operation pending while continuing authorized implementation and testing. Do not invent a paid fallback, claim eligibility verified, or ask the user to authorize the same deployment again. Keep contest-specific eligibility separate from code correctness.
findings.validation: A final receipt must show the evidence/decision and preserve any remaining uncertainty; generic successful deployment is not proof of eligibility.
